title: Temporal governor and regional eviction rules for query artifacts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a flexible retention system ("Temporal Governor") that enforces per-tenant and per-route TTLs for prompts, responses, request logs, and derived metrics with region-aware eviction semantics and automated evidence/reporting for audits.
acceptance_criteria: API supports per-route and per-tenant TTL overrides (seconds) with explicit residency tag; default fallbacks apply when unset
Persistent storages (S3/GCS/DB partitions) are tagged with residency and retention metadata and respect eviction schedules
Evidence export for any purge operation bundles hashes, timestamps, and associated policy IDs and is downloadable via Console and programmatic export
Retention preview simulator in Console shows projected storage delta and sample evidence for a given policy prior to applying it
Background purge job removes data deterministically within SLA and emits metrics + alerts on failures
Legal-hold flag prevents deletion and appears in evidence exports
End-to-end tests and load tests validate throughput impact <5% and purge window adherence
technical_notes: Introduce retention_ttl_seconds and residency_region fields on request artifacts' metadata; default service-level policy to live in config store
Persist metadata alongside artifacts in object store and index minimal keys in Postgres for efficient eviction query (tenant_id, route_id, created_at, residency)
Design purge worker as idempotent, chunked delete with watermarking and time-bounded leases to avoid double-deletes
Support two eviction modes: hard-delete (irreversible) and soft-delete (move to cold vault with retention proofs) depending on policy and legal hold
Evidence export format: compressed tar with manifest.json (policy_ids, hashes (SHA-256), signed timestamps, operator_id), plus audit-log pointer
Routing layer must honor residency_region when selecting storage and when exporting evidence for cross-region requests
Provide synchronous API validation for misconfigurations (e.g., set TTL shorter than minimum allowed for enterprise customers)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Enable TTL metadata write path for 5% of traffic; no deletions; collect metrics and retention simulator snapshots
Phase 2 (Staged): Enable purge worker in limited namespaces with soft-delete to cold vault; surface evidence export in Console as opt-in
Phase 3 (Regional Enforcement): Enforce residency-aware deletions in EU/US regions and enable per-tenant overrides via Console
Phase 4 (GA): Full enforcement, release documentation, and run customer migration jobs for tenants requiring historical truncation
migration_steps: Backfill existing artifacts with default retention policy and inferred residency (best-effort by storage region); record backfill job ID in manifest
Run retention-simulator across tenant samples to estimate storage reduction and evidence volume
For tenants with custom policies, migrate policy assignments and schedule in priority order
Perform a final dry-run export that produces evidence bundles without deleting any data and invite compliance team to review
risks: Accidental data loss if TTL logic is misapplied or backfill writes incorrect metadata
Cross-region consistency issues when requests route through global caches leading to premature eviction
Performance regression during large-scale backfills or purge windows impacting tail latency
Legal-hold not honored due to metadata race conditions causing compliance exposure
Complexity in evidence signing and long-term verifiability across key rotations
